papers.title: GETS: Ensemble Temperature Scaling for Calibration in Graph Neural Networks
papers.publication_status: ICLR2025Spotlight as stated by arXivmetadata and pinned authorREADME. Official forum/browser challenge and API403 prevented accepted-version audit.
papers.method_read_status: complete relevant paper method §§3–4 and selected method/setup appendices; bounded pinned author source; not full paper
papers.paper_operation: One pretrained classifier gives logits z. Multiple graph calibration experts process logits/features/degree inputs. Noisy top-k softmax determines node weights. Expert calibrated outputs are mixed; calibration is fitted with NLL on VALID. Paper motivates scalar node temperature and claims preserved accuracy.
papers.source_operation: GCN/GAT/GIN experts output C values per node. Gate reads [projected_features,base_logits]. Weighted expert-vector output t_ic is combined first, then z_ic is multiplied by softplus(t_ic). CV-squared importance/load regularization balances usage. All experts execute despite top-k output weights. The same cached no-grad base logits feed the calibrator.
source_prose_discrepancies: C-class output scales can change argmax, unlike scalar positive temperature. No native accuracy-preservation qualification.
Code computes every expert; top-k does not provide conditional expert execution. No efficiency result transferred.
Paper gate input refers to expert hidden output; source gate input is projected raw features plus base logits.
Source fit_calibration fits on masks[1]=VALID and selects calibration loss on masks[0]=TRAIN; base checkpoint is already selected using VALID.
papers.relationship_to_dense_member_weighting: Direct graph-context supervised postprocessing and mixture ancestry. Native source combines calibration vectors for one base predictor, not separately competent frozen-bank predictions. expert_select=M permits dense weights; sparse/dense gate choice provides no novelty boundary.
papers.relationship_to_residual_moment_transpor: No observed member-error Gram field or PSD moment diffusion in complete relevant method/source scopes. CV-squared term concerns expert usage, not residual covariance.
papers.relationship_to_hidden_fusion: Concatenates contextual inputs and gates expert calibration vectors; no fusion of a distinct predictor bank’s hidden representations into a common label decoder.
limitations: No code import/execution, model/data access, empirical result adoption, target reproduction or runtime qualification.
No official accepted-PDF method equivalence certificate.
Native fitting opportunity differs from TRAIN-only prospective fusion.
papers.closest_comparator_role: If a later supported accuracy screen needs it, use a small graph-conditioned class-vector scaler with matched supervision; do not silently call the inspected native method accuracy-preserving or adopt a new gate grid.

papers.title: Adapt, Agree, Aggregate: Semi-Supervised Ensemble Labeling for Graph Convolutional Networks
papers.publication_status: Publisher preview confirms Int.J.Mach.Learn.&Cyber.17,262(2026), version of record2026-04-24; accepted2026-02-22. Full published body unavailable.
papers.method_read_status: complete relevant preprint method §4/Algorithm1, notation and selected setup/parameter prose; not full paper; published preview only abstract/metadata
papers.operation: Independent initialized GCNs receive independently edge-dropped graph views. Each predicts high-confidence pseudo-label nodes. A global intersection/union ratio of high-confidence-node sets controls per-model random training-subset ratio and threshold update. A separate consensus GCN on the original graph trains on majority-vote labels for nodes meeting class-agreement threshold. beta=1 in native experiments means unanimity, including low-confidence unanimous nodes. Algorithm returns the single consensus GCN.

exact_method_objects.consensus: Vcons={u:Agree(u)>=beta*k}; majority-vote targets; CE to a separate GCN; beta=1

papers.relationship_to_dense_member_weighting: Ensemble pseudo-label selection and student/consensus training ancestry. No served dense member weights in complete §4/Algorithm1.
papers.relationship_to_residual_moment_transpor: Agreement ratio is confidence-set membership, not labeled residual cross-moments or graph diffusion of them.
papers.relationship_to_hidden_fusion: Original features/graph feed separate GCNs; ensemble information enters consensus targets, not concatenated member hidden states.
important_limits: High-confidence-set Jaccard can equal1 while models confidently predict different classes; the ratio does not measure agreement on labels. Native consensus class agreement is a separate step.
Shared wrong predictions can be unanimous; reliability/confirmation-bias claims are not guarantees.
Algorithm ratio is a fraction called subset size; count conversion, empty union, bootstrap, threshold clipping and ties unspecified in read scope.
Algorithm random-subsets L union Lpseudo, whereas prose emphasizes random subsets of high-confidence nodes; protection of original labeled supervision unresolved.
Linked author repo https://github.com/mabdolali/selfsupervised_GNN returnsHEAD404; no source/native qualification.
Publisher abstract matches the theme and authors; exact published equation/algorithm equality is unverified.
Reported result/configuration prose was textually exposed; no numerical result or empirical gain adopted.
papers.attribution_consequence: Credit augmented graph ensembles, agreement-controlled self-training and a served consensus model. No new consensus/disagreement principle is established by the proposal.
